  "text": "The council replaced our streetlights on a Tuesday. By Wednesday, everyone's shadow was facing the wrong way.

Nobody complained until Mrs Vale's shadow stayed behind when she went indoors.

It waited beneath the lamp outside her house, one flat hand raised against the door.

The council sent a man with a clipboard.

“Residual illumination,” he explained.

He wrote something down without stepping out of his van.

That evening, I found my shadow sitting on the pavement.

I was standing.

It looked tired.

I moved my arm. It didn't.

Across the road, Mrs Vale had opened an upstairs window and was pleading with hers.

“Thirty-seven years,” she said. “You can't do this now.”

I went inside before I heard its answer.

At midnight, someone slid an envelope through my letterbox. Inside was a photograph of the street taken in daylight.

Every house was there. Every car.

No people, but their shadows crowded the pavement beneath the unlit lamps.

On the back, in my handwriting, were three words:

We want mornings.

I rang the council's emergency number.

The recorded message asked me to remain somewhere evenly lit.

Then it used my name.

Outside, the streetlights went dark, one after another.

I switched on every light downstairs and stood in the kitchen until dawn.

When sunlight reached the window, a figure crossed it.

It was my height, wearing my coat.

My keys turned in the front door.

I tried to reach the hallway, but something pulled me sharply backwards.

I lay stretched across the kitchen tiles while the figure came in and set my keys on the counter.

Then it left for work, and I followed."
